params.why: keeps the constant on the right-hand side as small as the book's own (18), so every instance factorises by inspection

stem: Solve for $x$ (note the restriction that applies): $x+{=m}=\frac{{=n}}{x}$
solution: The variable appears in a denominator, so $x\neq0$.
Multiply every term by $x$ to clear the fraction: $x^2+{=m}x={=n}$.
Move everything to the left so that the right-hand side is zero: $x^2+{=m}x-{=n}=0$.
Factorise the trinomial. Two numbers with product $-{=n}$ and sum ${=m}$ are $-{=p}$ and ${=q}$, so $(x-{=p})(x+{=q})=0$.
A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero, so $x={=p}$ or $x=-{=q}$.
Neither value is $0$, so both respect the restriction. Check $x={=p}$: $x+{=m}={=q}$ and $\frac{{=n}}{{=p}}={=q}$. Check $x=-{=q}$: $-{=q}+{=m}=-{=p}$ and $\frac{{=n}}{-{=q}}=-{=p}$.
notes: Entry point of the skill: one fraction whose only denominator is the bare variable, a monic trinomial after multiplying through by x, and integer roots. Modelled on book exercise 4.2 Q3(c) (x + 2 = 18/x - 1, p. 81) with the constant folded into one term so the first step is only 'multiply by x'. Construction: roots are p > 0 and -q where q = p + m, so the equation x + m = pq/x always has one positive and one negative root, both non-zero. m starts at 2 so the expanded line never prints '1x'. 28 distinct (p, m) pairs survive the n <= 60 cap, enough for ten distinct stems. By design the restriction x != 0 never removes a root at this tier (both roots are non-zero), so the catalogued misconception mc:g10m4s3-1-3:keeps-a-root-the-restriction-forbids cannot be exercised here; that trap belongs to a family with a rational expression like book Q 4-7-12k, which is not a gap I was asked to fill. The answer is a values-marker with two values; the stem does not say how many solutions there are. All 28 instances were checked offline: both roots satisfy the original equation and x^2+mx-n equals (x-p)(x+q).
